p2b_exemplars.text: A useful distinction separates three cases of readiness. In the first case there is only bare capacity: a blank instrument that could in principle record a signal but currently records nothing at all. The second case adds a settled disposition: the instrument has been calibrated and now stands ready to measure, though it is not measuring at this moment. The third case is the exercise itself: the calibrated instrument actively taking a reading. The middle case is the pivot, because a settled readiness is already a kind of latent activity.

p5_evidence.content: This fixture reads Aristotle's first/second actuality distinction through the English-speaker example (child / silent bilingual / speaking bilingual).
Heidegger's GA18 reading treats logos as grounded in pathos; Gross articulates this as affect being the condition for rational discourse.
Possible link to Rickert's ambience claim — do not assert flatly.

p6_semantics: Rhetorical ontology: being-moved (affectability) as ontological condition; first vs second actuality; soul as capacity-form, not identity.
p7_foundation: Aristotle presents the soul as the form of a natural body having life potentially within it; the first actuality is a capacity for the second. Affectability grounds the possibility of discourse.
